project_description: Dogfood project: the requirements and verification for OpenV's AI context release — stable refs, the AI map, and context bundles — authored in OpenV itself. Import this project and run get_project_map against it to see the feature describe itself.

artifacts.title: AI Context Surface
artifacts.body: Make OpenV the most token-efficient requirements source for any coding agent: short stable addresses, a compact whole-project map, and one-call context bundles.

artifacts.title: Why token efficiency is a feature
artifacts.body: Agents pay for context in tokens and latency. A UUID is ~10 meaningless tokens; a full artifact listing repeats keys and metadata the agent never uses. The AI context surface exists so an agent can orient on a whole project for a few thousand tokens and then fetch only the bodies it needs.

artifacts.title: Stable short refs
artifacts.body: Every artifact shall carry a stable short ref of the form PREFIX-NUMBER (e.g. REQ-12), assigned on creation, unique among a project's current artifacts, and constant across the artifact's versions.

artifacts.title: Refs survive export/import round-trips
artifacts.body: Importing an exported project into a new project shall preserve each artifact's ref, so external references (documents, commit messages, code trace markers) stay valid. Imports into an existing project shall assign fresh refs to avoid collisions.

artifacts.title: AI map
artifacts.body: The system shall render a whole project as a compact outline — one line per artifact with ref, title, non-draft status, hierarchy by indentation, and inline link annotations in both directions — with no artifact bodies, via API endpoint and agent tool.

artifacts.title: Release-stamped maps
artifacts.body: The AI map shall be renderable from any baseline's snapshot, stamped with the baseline's name, id, and capture time, so every release version produces a versioned map suitable for committing into a code repository (e.g. .openv/requirements.md).

artifacts.title: One-call context bundles
artifacts.body: An agent shall be able to fetch, in a single tool call addressed by ref or id: an artifact's full body, its ancestor path, its children, and every linked artifact with link type, direction, suspect flag, and a short excerpt.

artifacts.title: Ref addressing in agent tools
artifacts.body: Agent tools that accept an artifact id shall also accept a stable ref (with a project id for scoping), and trimmed tool outputs (tree, search) shall include refs.

artifacts.title: Repo export of the map
artifacts.body: PLANNED: a one-command export shall write the release-stamped AI map into a code repository as .openv/requirements.md, so any coding agent has requirements context with zero round trips.

artifacts.title: Code trace markers
artifacts.body: PLANNED: source comments of the form 'Implements: REQ-12' shall be scannable into proposed implements-links, giving coverage-from-code.

artifacts.title: Ref assignment, versioning, and counters
artifacts.body: Automated: TestArtifactRefAssignment (internal/persistence/postgres) — sequential per-project/per-prefix assignment, refs constant across versions, preset refs preserved with counters advanced past them.

artifacts.title: Backfill of pre-ref databases
artifacts.body: Automated: TestArtifactRefBackfill — migration 0018 stamps existing artifacts in stable tree order and seeds counters so numbering continues.

artifacts.title: AI map rendering
artifacts.body: Automated: TestBuildAIMap and TestProjectAIMapHandler (internal/api) — hierarchy, refs, draft-status omission, bidirectional link annotations, suspect marks, pre-ref fallback, live and baseline sources, provenance stamping, foreign-baseline 404.

artifacts.title: Context bundle and ref addressing
artifacts.body: Automated: TestGetContext, TestGetArtifactByRef, TestGetProjectMap (internal/mcp) — bundle contents, neighbor excerpt truncation, suspect marks, ref resolution with and without project_id, map proxying with baseline_id.
